question: I refer to the recent case of the Danish influencer Elvira Pitzner, who is being detained in Dubai on a charge of adultery, punishable there by up to several years’ imprisonment, having left her former Arab partner for another man.

Does the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (VP/HR) agree that the legal position of EU citizens is being challenged in particular in Arab countries, whose Islamist legislation is fundamentally different from our European rule-of-law principles, and, if he does, will the VP/HR take the necessary action against the countries in question so as to ensure that they observe the basic rights of EU citizens, including, for example, by revoking trade and visa agreements with countries that seriously violate EU citizens’ fundamental rights?
answer: Human rights represent a core dimension of EU engagement with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and are regularly raised by the EU and its Member States at all levels with Emirati officials, as well as in multilateral fora.

In particular, in the context of the regular annual EU-UAE human rights dialogue, the two sides have the opportunity for an indepth exchange on human rights topics in a constructive and respectful manner. In this context, the EU has insisted that human rights of nationals and foreigners in the UAE should be fully respected.

The last round of human rights dialogue with the UAE took place in Brussels on 16 January 2024 (1). The responsibility for consular protection and assistance for EU citizen lies primarily with the respective Member States. In the framework of local consular cooperation, the EU delegation in Abu Dhabi coordinates closely with the relevant Member States embassies and stands ready to offer support as needed.
